solution noun

the answer to a puzzle

also answer (to a riddle), solve a riddle, solution (in maths)

classical

Gell. 18.2.6: captiōnis sophisticae solūtiō
Sen. Ben. 2.34.1 (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 382

solūtiō, solūtiōnis f.

noun, third declension · Declension on Wiktionary

the solution (of a puzzle, a riddle, an argument)

Lewis & Short: “a solution, explanation” (Seneca, Gellius); in Cicero mostly a payment. To solve: solvere (see problem, to be solved).

Other words

  • explicātiō, explicātiōnis f. — an unravelling, an explanation

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. N. D. 3.62: explicātiō fābulārum et ēnōdātiō nōminum (Lewis & Short) · Declension on Wiktionary

Examples

  • aut dēcrētī cujuspiam ex philosophiā perperam invulgātī pūrgātiō, aut captiōnis sophisticae solūtiō

    or clearing up some philosophical doctrine wrongly spread about, or the solution of a sophist’s catchGell. 18.2.6

See also problem, riddle, answer, solution.

SourcesLewis & Short: solutio · Lewis & Short: explicatio
